title: Ants Work Together
learning_objectives: Learn that ants live in groups with different jobs
Explain how ants find food using a scent trail

factual_claims.claim: Ants live together in large groups called colonies.
factual_claims.source: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History, 'Ants' (naturalhistory.si.edu); Britannica Kids, 'Ant'

factual_claims.claim: Most ants in a colony are workers; one or a few queens lay the eggs.
factual_claims.source: Britannica Kids, 'Ant'; Arizona State University 'Ask A Biologist: Ant colony'

factual_claims.claim: Ants leave a chemical scent (pheromone) trail that other ants follow to food.
factual_claims.source: ASU Ask A Biologist, 'Ants and pheromones'; Britannica, 'Pheromone'

factual_claims.claim: Ants can carry objects many times their own body weight.
factual_claims.source: Britannica Kids, 'Ant' (ants lift many times their weight); Smithsonian 'Ants'

factual_claims.claim: Ants use their antennae to touch and smell.
factual_claims.source: Britannica Kids, 'Ant' (antennae used for smell and touch)

parent_prompts: Before: have you seen a line of ants? Where were they going?
After page 4: how do the other ants know where the food is?
After: what job would you want in an ant colony?

pages.text: Look down at a crack in the path. A line of ants is marching. Where are they going, and how do they know the way?
pages.illustration_brief: Close view of a stone path crack with a line of small black ants.
pages.audio_script: Look down at a crack in the path. A line of ants is marching. Where are they going, and how do they know the way?
pages.image_alt: Close view of a stone path crack with a line of small black ants.

pages.text: Ants do not live alone. They live in a big group called a colony. A colony can have thousands of ants in one nest.
pages.illustration_brief: Cross-section of an ant nest underground with tunnels and chambers full of ants.
pages.audio_script: Ants do not live alone. They live in a big group called a colony. A colony can have thousands of ants in one nest.

vocabulary.definition: A big group of animals of one kind living together.
vocabulary.example: The ant colony lives under the tree.

pages.image_alt: Cross-section of an ant nest underground with tunnels and chambers.

pages.text: Every ant has a job. The queen lays the eggs. Worker ants find food, dig tunnels and look after the babies.
pages.illustration_brief: One larger ant beside a pile of tiny eggs; smaller ants carrying crumbs and digging.
pages.audio_script: Every ant has a job. The queen lays the eggs. Worker ants find food, dig tunnels and look after the babies.
pages.image_alt: One larger ant beside a pile of tiny eggs; smaller ants carrying crumbs and digging.

pages.text: When a worker finds food, she walks home and leaves a smell on the ground. Other ants follow the smell trail, all the way to the food.
pages.illustration_brief: An ant walking from a crumb back toward the nest with a faint dotted trail behind it; other ants starting to follow.
pages.audio_script: When a worker finds food, she walks home and leaves a smell on the ground. Other ants follow the smell trail, all the way to the food.

vocabulary.definition: A line of marks or smells that shows which way to go.
vocabulary.example: We followed the trail through the park.

pages.image_alt: An ant walking from a crumb back toward the nest with a faint dotted trail; others following.

pages.text: Ants smell and touch with two feelers on their heads. They are called antennae. Ants tap antennae to say hello.
pages.illustration_brief: Two ants face to face, antennae touching.
pages.audio_script: Ants smell and touch with two feelers on their heads. They are called antennae. Ants tap antennae to say hello.

vocabulary.definition: The two thin feelers on an insect's head.

pages.image_alt: Two ants face to face, antennae touching.

pages.text: Ants are small but strong. One ant can carry a crumb many times heavier than itself. Many ants can carry a whole leaf together.
pages.illustration_brief: Several ants carrying a leaf piece far bigger than themselves.
pages.audio_script: Ants are small but strong. One ant can carry a crumb many times heavier than itself. Many ants can carry a whole leaf together.
pages.image_alt: Several ants carrying a leaf piece far bigger than themselves.

pages.text: That is why the line marches. One ant found food, left a trail, and the whole colony is helping to bring it home.
pages.illustration_brief: The ant line again, now with crumbs being carried toward a hole.
pages.audio_script: That is why the line marches. One ant found food, left a trail, and the whole colony is helping to bring it home.
pages.image_alt: The ant line again, now with crumbs being carried toward a hole.

pages.text: Next time you see a line of ants, watch where it starts and where it ends. You are watching a team at work.
pages.illustration_brief: A child crouched watching the ant line with a magnifying glass.
pages.audio_script: Next time you see a line of ants, watch where it starts and where it ends. You are watching a team at work.
pages.image_alt: A child crouched watching the ant line with a magnifying glass.
